title: Pedestrian killed in crash involving off-duty Vancouver police officer
summary: A pedestrian was killed in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood Friday morning in a crash involving an off-duty police officer.

image.caption: Vancouver police officers gather at the scene of a fatal crash at Main Street and East Broadway on Friday. (Shawn Foss/CBC)

blocks.text: A pedestrian was killed in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood Friday morning in a crash involving an off-duty police officer.
Independent Investigations Office to investigate fatal collision at Main Street and East Broadway
The officer was sent to hospital in critical but stable condition.
Vancouver police Supt. Dale Weidman said the officer was driving their personal vehicle northbound on Main Street at approximately 9:30 a.m. PT when the crash happened.
The officer crossed the intersection at Broadway and struck a light pole on the northwest corner of the intersection, hitting a pedestrian, Weidman said.
The pedestrian, a woman believed to be in her 40s, died at the scene. Police say she was a local resident.
Weidman said the driver, a 49-year-old off-duty Vancouver police officer who has been with the department for two years, was alone in the vehicle.
Police say the investigation is in its early stages and have not determined what caused the vehicle to leave its path and strike the pole.
The Independent Investigations Office of B.C. (IIO), which investigates incidents involving police officers that result in death or serious injury, will take over the investigation.
B.C. Emergency Health Services said it received a call about the collision at 9:26 a.m.
Two ambulances staffed by primary care paramedics, three ambulances staffed by advanced care paramedics and a paramedic supervisor responded.
